title: Drowning is silent. Layer up.
intro: Drowning is the #1 cause of death for children ages 1 to 4. It happens in seconds, usually with no splash and no cry for help, and it’s preventable.

layersTitle: No single layer is enough. Stack them.

layers.name: Watch
layers.text: Name one Water Watcher. Stay within arm’s reach of toddlers. Phones down.

layers.name: Fence
layers.text: A fence on all four sides of the pool, with a gate that closes and latches by itself.

layers.name: Alarms
layers.text: On every door to the pool, plus a pool alarm. Keep them on, especially with guests.

layers.name: Empty it
layers.text: Buckets, coolers, kiddie pools and tubs. Young children can drown in an inch or two of water.

layers.name: Swim skills
layers.text: Lessons after the first birthday (we recommend ISR self-rescue). They add to the other layers, never replace them.

layers.name: Life jackets
layers.text: U.S. Coast Guard-approved at lakes, rivers and the beach. Water wings and floaties are toys.

layers.name: Be ready
layers.text: Learn infant and child CPR. If a child is missing, check the water first. Call 911.

story: Our little brother Adam was 14 months old when he slipped out during a busy family week and into our backyard pool. He was out of sight for about three minutes. He survived, with a severe brain injury, and he’s still the heart of our family. We started Because of ADAM so other families learn the layers before it happens to them.
quote: A four-sided pool fence with a self-closing gate would have saved him.
